When a molecule leaves the surface and enters the liquid interior, another molecule can take its place.
Macroscopic equilibrium means neither that every molecule is motionless nor that its instantaneous resultant force is always zero.
resolvedSectionBreaks.after:
In the simplified nearest-neighbor model used by the textbook, attraction and repulsion together produce larger average molecular separations in the surface layer, and a correspondingly lower density than in the liquid interior.
This compares average structure, not every instantaneous position during thermal motion.
